APPROACH IN THE TENTH FIVE YEAR PLAN AND ANALYSIS OF THE ANNUAL PLAN 
 2006-07
        The Committee was not satisfied with the replies of the Department of Tourism for poor utilization of funds
 in the first three quarters of the financial year. The Committee feels that the reasons put-forth by the
 Department of Tourism are routine in nature and remedial measures may be taken in advance. The Committee
 therefore, recommends the Department of Tourism that some fool proof method be devised for having
 uniformity in expenditure throughout the year and State/UT Governments may also be impressed upon for
 timely submission of project proposals and utilization certificates/completion certificates for release of funds
 through central financial assistance. The Committee is also surprised to note that the ATR have been furnished
 to the Committee on 21st September 2006 and yet it does not contain any information about actual number of
 project proposals received in time, how many are pending for consideration and how many
 utilization/completion certificates were issued thereon.
        The Committee notes the reply and hopes that the plan outlay of the Department of Tourism would be
 increased so that the vast tourism potential available in the country could be exploited optimally to create world
 class and dependable tourism product and infrastructure.                                                                      
                                                                                                                                            (Paras 7 and 10)
PRODUCT/INFRASTRUCTURE DEVELOPMENT
(a)    Major Destination and Circuit Development
        The Committee notes that the Department of Tourism is concentrating on improvement/ development of
 existing as well as new tourism products to world-class standards for which the Government has proposed to
 increase the Central financial assistance to State/ Union Territory for development of tourism destinations and
 circuits in the country. The Committee is of the opinion that if the country has to improve its vast tourism
 potential to world class standard, it requires larger flow of funds for development of infrastructure both from
 Government and private sector. The Committee therefore, recommends the Government to explore the
 possibilities for creating and promoting the tourism infrastructure projects in public-private partnership and
 approach the Ministry of Finance for releasing funds for bridging the infrastructure gap at important
 destinations besides resorting to aggressive marketing of tourism products through print and electronic media.
 World wide web campaigns should also be launched for augmenting incoming tourist traffic flow from abroad.
        The Committee notes that the Department of Tourism is taking up the matter with the Ministry of Shipping,
 Road Transport and Highways for improving the connectivity to the important tourist destinations including
 World Heritage Sites, Buddhist Sites through Central Road Fund Scheme. The Committee recommends the
 Department of Tourism to pursue vigourously the matter with the Ministry of Shipping, Road, Transport and
 Highways. The Committee also desires the Department of Tourism to inform the Committee about the progress
 in the matter.
        The Committee is constrained to note that out of the 2526 sanctioned projects during Eight and Ninth Five
 Year Plan periods only 1830 projects have been completed as on date. Similarly, out of the 895 sanctioned
 projects during the Tenth Five Year Plan only 285 projects have since been completed. The Committee feels that
 there is lack of co-ordination and monitoring of projects between the Department of Tourism and State/UT
 Governments and this needs to be strengthened and in the future corrective measures may be taken so that more
 and more sanctioned projects may be completed in time.
        The Committee notes the reply and recommends the Department of Tourism to have close co-ordination
 with the implementing agencies viz., ITDC, CPWD, ASI etc., for timely completion of tourism projects. This way
 the Department of Tourism will not only achieve the physical and financial targets but also help in
 creation/improvement of tourism infrastructure.
                                                                                                                              (Paras 16, 19, 24 and 28)
(b)    Rural Tourism
        The Committee notes that the Department of Tourism is making efforts to boost rural tourism
 infrastructure in the country. The Committee also notes that during 2006-07, the Department of Tourism has
 already identified 25 villages in consultation with the State/UT Governments for development of rural tourism
 sites in the country. The Committee expects that the promotion of rural tourism can lead to increased tourist
 arrivals to rural sites and in the process can strengthen rural livelihoods including benefit to the youth through
 income from visitor handling services apart from income through art and craft activities.

 DEVELOPMENT
        The Committee notes that with the growing demand of skilled/trained manpower in the hospitality industry,
 the Department of Tourism has proposed to set up three more Institutes of Hotel Management at Mohali,
 Jammu and Daman & Diu. The Committee also notes that the Department of Tourism has also approved the

 courses. The Committee hopes that more and more private institutes will come forward for affiliation and
 contribute towards the training efforts in Human Resources Development.
        The Committee notes that the guidelines for affiliation of the existing private managed hospitality institutes
 has been notified by the National Council for Hotel Management and Catering Technology and the matter to
 grant statutory/deemed university status to National Council for Hotel Management and Catering Technology is

 Technology with the Ministry of Human Resource Development for having uniform standards in training and
 other infrastructure facilities.                                                                                         (Paras 48 and 51)

        The Committee notes that the Department of Tourism is making efforts for overcoming the problem of low
 utilization of approved outlays for the domestic tourism and publicity by starting the early selection process of

 amount.        (Para 54)
OVERSEAS PROMOTION AND PUBLICITY INCLUDING MARKING DEVELOPMENT ASSISTANCE
        The Committee notes that India Tourism offices overseas prepare their marketing and promotional
 activities on the basis of the feedback received from the market and project India accordingly. However, the
 Committee is constrained to note that though the allocation for overseas promotion and publicity has been
 enhanced considerably but it is much less if compared to amount spent by other countries. The Committee
 recommends the Department of Tourism to approach the Planning Commission for increase in allocation under
 the head, so that there is no let in efforts to project India as a preferred tourism and business destination and to
 increase India’s share of the total global tourism market.
        The Committee notes that the Department of Tourism is making series of promotional activities through its
 overseas offices for increasing the visibility of Indian tourism products and to promote India as a tourist
 destination in the emerging tourism markets of East Asia and South East Asia. The Committee recommends that
 these promotional activities should continue to be carried out in tourists generating overseas markets to
 showcase and effectively promote the unique and competitive Indian tourism products and destinations in the
 new emerging global markets.                                                                                        (Paras 62 and 67)

REPORT
        This Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Government on the .observations
 recommendations as contained in its One Hundred and Fifth Report on Demands for Grants (2006-07) (Demand No.
 84) of the Department of Shipping, which was presented to the Parliament on  22nd May 2006.
2.     Action Taken Replies have been received from the Government on 3rd November, 2006 in respect of all the
 observations/recommendations contained in the Report. These have been categorized as follows:—
            (i)     Recommendations/observations that have been accepted by the Government:
                    Para Nos. 9, 19, 21, 23, 27, 42 and 73                                                                              Total-7
            (ii)    Recommendations/observations which the Committee do not desire to pursue in view of the Government replies:
                    Para Nos. 34 and 39                                                                                                        Total-2
            (iii)   Recommendations/observations in respect of which replies of the Government have not been accepted by the Committee:
                    Para Nos. 15 and 60                                                                                                        Total-2
            (iv)   Recommendations/ observations in respect of which final replies of the Government are still awaited:
                    Para Nos. 46, 50, 55 and 56                                                                                             Total-4
3.     The Committee desires that final replies in respect of the recommendations, which have been categorized as
 interim replies by the Committee should be furnished to it at the earliest.
4.     On scrutiny of the Action Taken Replies, the Committee has made observations on each item of the action
 taken/proposed to be taken by the Department of Shipping. The recommendations of the Committee contained in the
 One Hundred Fifth Report, action taken thereon by the Government and recommendations/observations of the
 Committee on each item of action taken have been given in the succeeding paragraphs.
ANALYSIS OF ANNUAL PLAN 2006-07
(Recommendation at Para 9)
5. The Committee notes that in the annual plan 2005-06, the outlay of Department of Shipping was reduced from
 Rs.2419.66 crore to Rs.2333.71 crore at RE stage. The reduction had been both in the Gross Budgetary Support
 as well as IEBR component. As far as the reasons for under utilization of funds is concerned, the Committee
 finds that inadequate preparedness on the part of executing authorities and procedural rigidity for approval of
 scheme are main culprits for under utilization of funds. Therefore, the Committee recommends that Department
 of Shipping should not only have to do away the procedural hurdles leading to delay in processing and
 approving the scheme but also have to adopt proactive approach while preparing the scheme. In BE 2006-07, an
 outlay of Rs.3263.19 crore  has been provided which consists of a Gross Budgetary Support of Rs.740.88 crore
 and IEBR of Rs.2522.31 crore , which is almost 40 per cent over and above the amount of Rs.2419.66 crore
 allocated in BE 2005-06. The Committee expects that the increase in the plan outlay will have a positive effect of
 the schemes/projects of the Department of Shipping. The Committee is of the view that complete utilization of
 the enhanced allocation will help effective implementation of the schemes/performance undertaken by the
 Department of Shipping. The Committee recommends that the Government should increase the outlay of
 Department of Shipping and if need be, supplement the allocation by increasing the Gross Budgetary Support to
 the Department of Shipping.
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
6.     The views and recommendations of the hon’ble Committee are noted.
PORT SECTOR
(Recommendation at Para 15)
7.     The committee is not satisfied with the reasons given by the Department of Shipping for shortfall in the
 utilization of the approved outlay and feels that the reasons could have been anticipated in advance by the
 Department of Shipping, this clearly shows the lack of pro-active approach on the part of the Department. The
 Committee is perturbed to note that there has been a huge shortfall in the utilization of Funds vis-a­-vis
 approved outlay for the Port Sector. In BE 2005-06, an outlay of Rs. 1163.75 crore comprising of Rs.280.24 crore
 Gross Budgetary Support and Rs.883.21 crore IEBR was provided for the Port Sector. As against this, the actual
 expenditure is anticipated to be Rs.668.33 crore . The Committee feels that while proposing the Plan Outlay, the
 Department of Shipping had not done strategic planning and observes that there is a

PARLIAMENT OF INDIA
file:///C/Users/user/Desktop/pri/Committee%20on%20Transport,%20Tourism%20and%20Culture/114.htm[28-08-2018 13:24:01]
 mismatch in the physical and financial projections which is not explicable. The Committee, therefore,
 recommends that Government should evolve a monitoring mechanism to ensure proper utilization of the
 approved outlay, making officials accountable for failure, transparency in implementation process logistical
 coordination and do away with the procedural rigidities to avoid delay and cost overrun so that the budgeted
 outlay is utilized optimally.
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
8.     The Annual Plan proposal are formulated about five to six months in advance before the commencement of the
 Annual Plan period after factoring in the anticipated expenditure during the current year and the assessed requirements
 in the ensuing Annual Plan year for on­ going projects and taking into account the assessed requirement of funds for
 the new projects to be taken up during that year. Requirement of funds at the Revised Estimates stage is projected after

CONTAINERIZATION IN MAJOR PORTS
(Recommendation at Para 27)
22.   The Committee observes that the international trade is witnessing an increasing trend towards
 containerization. However, the Committee is constrained to note that the major ports did not-significantly
 contribute to export-import trade and about 70 percent of containers are trans-shipped at neighborhood
 international Ports such as, Colombo, Dubai and Singapore Ports, making thereby India’s export costlier and
 imports less competitive. The Committee, therefore, recommends that Government should establish hub ports in
 the country preferably, in East and West Coast for trans-shipment of containerized cargo for the growth of sea-
borne overseas trade and economic development.
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
23.   Dedicated capacities for handling containerized cargo is available in seven major ports, namely, Kolkata Port (both
 at Kolkata Dock Systems and Haldia Dock Complex), Visakhapatnam Port, Chennai Port, Tuticorin Port, Cochin Port,
 Mumbai Port and Jawaharlal Nehru Port. The total capacity available at these seven ports is 5.18 million Twenty Feet
 Equivalent Units (TEUs).
24.   A hub port is required to fulfil certain requirements such as required volume of traffic, proximity to international
 routes and markets, long waterfront, deep draught, good road/rail connectivity, large backup area and supporting
 hinterland. In India, Jawaharlal Nehru Port on the west coast with the northern and north-western regions of India and
 Chennai Port on the east coast with the southern and south-east regions of India as their main hinterland are operating
 as regional hub ports. About 92 per cent of container cargo at Jawaharlal  Nehru Port and about 44 per cent of container
 cargo at Chennai Port during 2005-06 were ‘direct to destination’ cargoes without involving transhipment in any port
 abroad. About 65 per cent of container cargo at Tuticorin Port was also direct to destination. Overall, about 66 per cent
 of container cargo handled in the major ports during 2005-06 were direct to destination.
25.   Chennai  Port has adequate draft to handle majority of modern large size container vessels visiting India. One
 container terminal at Chennai Port with a capacity for handling one million Twenty Feet Equivalent Units (TEUs) per
 annum is already operational. Selection of a bidder for development, operation and management of a second container
 terminal at the port on Build, Operate and Transfer (BOT) basis is under finalization. After completion of the second
 container terminal, Chennai Port will have capacity for handling 1.8 million TEUs per annum. Projects for improving
 connectivity from the port to its hinterland have also been planned.
26.   At Jawaharlal Nehru Port, Two container terminals and one shallow water berth with a capacity for handling 2.55
 million TEUs per annum are already operational in the port. The third container terminal at the port is currently under
 construction and is expected to be fully operational in October, 2006. Additional container handling capacity on
 account of the third container terminal in the port will be 1.3 million TEUs. Thus, on operationalisation  of the third
 container terminal, Jawaharlal Nehru Port will have a capacity for handling 3.85 million TEUs A proposal to deepen
 the entrance channel at an estimated cost of Rs.800 crore with a view to enhancing its draft has been approved by the
 Government. On completion of this project, the port will be able to receive large size vessels with carrying capacity
 upto 6000 TEUs using tidal window. Projects for improving rail and road connectivity from the port to its hinterland
 including construction of a dedicated rail freight corridor to Delhi have also been planned.
27.   Apart from the above, the Government has also approved the development of International Container
 Transshipment Terminal (ICTT) at Cochin Port on BOT basis. A Concession Agreement for the purpose has already
 been signed between the Cochin Port Trust and India Gateway Terminal Private Limited, a special purpose company
 formed by a consortium of Dubai Ports World and CONCOR. The project will be implemented in phases. On
 completion, the terminal will have capacity for handling 3 million TEUs. Under the agreement, the Port Trust will
 ensure provision of adequate draft in the channel so as to enable the ICTT to receive large size vessels with a carrying

FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
42.   The Committee notes that the Department of Shipping is taking up the matter with the Ministry of Finance
 for extending tonnage tax benefits to the vessels registered under Inland Vessels Act and Coasting Vessel Act.
 The Committee is unable to comprehend the reasons for delay in extending the benefits of tonnage tax to the
 vessels registered under Inland Vessels Act and Coasting Vessel Act. The Committee feels that the Government
 would not be able to develop the inland water transport and coastal vessel transport in the country, unless the
 benefit of tonnage tax and Section 33 AC of Income Tax Act were not granted to these vessels. In this regard, the
 Committee reiterates its earlier recommendations contained in 105th Report of the Committee, which is
 reproduced below:
“The Committee, therefore, recommends the Department of Shipping to vigorously pursue the matter
 with the Ministry of Finance for inclusion of the Vessels registered under Inland Vessels and Coastal
 Vessels Acts under the tonnage tax regime so as to unfold the infrastructure potential of IWT sector
 with the growth of the Indian economy.”
CALCUTTA DOCK LABOUR BOARD
(Recommendation at Para 46)
43.   The Committee notes with anguish that a proposal for release of one time grant of Rs.733.28 crore  to
 Calcutta Dock Labour Board is pending for a long time but has not yet been approved. The Committee is of the
 view that it is the liability of the Government to pay the pension and the pensionary dues in time and it will be
 solely discriminatory on the part of the Government to withhold the pension and pensionary benefits of the
 employees of the Calcutta Dock Labour Board. The Committee is unable to comprehend as to how these
 pensioners will sustain in the absence of any financial support. The Committee feels that the injustice is being
 meted out to the pensioners of the Calcutta Dock Labour Board in the disbursement of pension and pensionary
 benefits, although the Board has been created by an Act of Parliament. The committee feels that in spite of the
 recommendations in earlier Reports also nothing has been done in the matter. The Committee, therefore, once
 again recommends that every effort should be made by the Department of Shipping for release of one time grant
 to meet the pensionary liabilities of employees of the Calcutta Dock Labour Board.
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
44.   For building a Pension Fund to meet the future pensionary liability of the Board, the Department had circulated a
 Cabinet Note seeking one time grant of Rs.734.93 crore from the Government of India. This amount was proposed to
 be used for the payment pf unpaid arrears of Rs.89.17 crore to CDLB pensioners and workers/employees, Rs.457.04
 crore towards Superannuation Fund Contribution and Rs. 188.72 crore for Fringe Benefit Tax. Subsequently,
 Department of Revenue made observations with regard to calculation of Fringe Benefit Tax. Accordingly, the Fringe
 Benefit Tax was increased to Rs. 192.50 crore and a revised Cabinet Note is under finalization for seeking a one time
 grant of Rs.738.71 crore from the Government of India.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
45.   The Committee is constrained to note that the Government is dilly-dallying the matter which has aggravated
 the problem of employees of Calcutta Dock Labour Board in getting the pension and pensionary benefits. The
 Committee feels that every delay in release of grant to Calcutta Dock Labour Board for payment of unpaid
 arrears and meeting the future superannuation liabilities of employees will burden the Government heavily, if
 not tackled now. The Committee is of the strong view that injustice.is being meted to the employees of Calcutta
 Dock Labour Board in the matter of payment of the pension and pensionary dues on time after retirement and
 recommends that the Government should come out with one time concrete proposal which would adequately
 address the total revenue requirement of employees of Calcutta Dock Labour Board instead of doing it in a
 piecemeal manner.
MISAPPROPRIATION OF SEAMEN’S PROVIDENT FUND
(Recommendation at Para 50)
46.   The Committee had taken up the matter of misappropriation of Seamen’s Provident Fund in its earlier
 reports also. The Committee however, is not happy with the lethargic approach of the Government in the
 matter. The Committee notes that the matter to recoup the shortage of Rs.92.78 crore  in Seamen’s Provident
 Fund is being looked into by the Group of Ministers. The Group of Ministers has sought certain clarifications
 from the Department of Shipping. The Committee recommends the Department of Shipping to provide the
 requisite information to Group of Ministers to enable them to take an early decision. The Committee would like
 to be apprised of the action taken in this regard.

48.   The Committee notes with dismay that the Government had not yet taken a final decision in the matter of
 recouping the shortage of Rs.92.78 crore  in Seamen’s’ Provident Fund so far. The Committee urges upon the
 Government that the hard earned money of Seamen’s which was being pilferaged in the scam because of faulty

(Recommendation at Para 55 and 56)
49.   The Committee feels that the university once created will not only augment the training facilities but also
 provide boost to the quality education in the field of Marine Training. The Committee notes that the draft
 Cabinet Note on the formation of Indian Maritime University has been circulated for inter-Ministerial
 consideration and after their comments, the proposal will be sent for consideration of the Cabinet. The
 Committee expects that the Cabinet will soon take a decision on the formation of the Maritime  University in the
 country to facilitate the Department of Shipping to introduce a Bill in the Parliament.
50.   The Committee, however, expresses its concern over the delay for establishment of Indian Maritime
 University. The Committee recommends the Department of Shipping to take steps to establish the Maritime
 University under Central Act in a time bound manner and adequate provisions for creation of pension fund and
 finalization of terms and conditions for the absorption of employees of Indian Institute of Maritime Studies

51.   The Cabinet Note was sent for consideration of Cabinet on 24.6.2006. However, Cabinet Sectt. has returned the
 proposal to get the Bill vetted by Ministry of Law and also to obtain the recommendations of Expenditure Finance
 Committee, which are being attended to. Ministry of Law has prepared a draft IMU Bill and sought comments of this
 Department as to whether it meets our requirement. It is being examined. Accordingly the DPR and EFC Note have

 placed before the Cabinet shortly.

52.   The Committee notes that the draft Indian Maritime University Bill has been prepared and is being
 examined in the Department of Shipping. The Committee further notes that the IMU Bill alongwith the
 recommendations of the Expenditure Finance Committee will be placed before the Cabinet shortly for
 consideration. The Committee therefore, urges upon the Government to take an early decision on the formation

(Recommendation at Para 60)
53.   The Committee expresses its displeasure over the manner in which the matter of CIWTC is being handled
 by the Government. The Committee feels that CIWTC can play an important role in development of the Inland
 Water Transport. The Committee observes that although substantial investment has been made for the
 infrastructure development in Inland Water Transport Sector but, still it is not a viable option and therefore,
 participation of private sector in utilization of the infrastructure is insignificant. The situation demands the
 bigger role of CIWTC as a lone-operator in the longer stretch of waterways. The Committee desires that till
 such time the infrastructure of IWT be fully ready for operation, the CIWTC with its existing infrastructure,
 capacity and manpower may be allowed to function for bridging the gap of development of IWT sector.
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
54.   The decision of the Government to disinvest CIWTC (minus RBD) is not likely to affect the role/activities of
 CIWTC. The disinvestment will result in change of shareholding pattern and in the nomenclature of the Corporation.
 The activities of transportation of cargo is likely to continue to be carried out by utilizing the existing fleet of vessels of
 the corporation. Hence, the Inland Water Transport activities are not likely to be affected by the disinvestment.

55.   The Committee does not see any merit in the decision of the Government for disinvestment of Central
 Inland Water Transport Corporation. The Committee is of the view that Inland Water Transport Sector cannot
 survive without Government investment in the infrastructure and CIWTC has to play the role of catalyst for
 that sector. The Committee recommends the Government to reconsider the decision for disinvestment of the
 Central Inland Water Transport Corporation for want of exploiting opportunity in the IWT Sector in the
 Country. The Committee further recommends that CIWTC be either merged with Kolkata Port Trust or be
 taken over by IWTA in order to further augment the infrastructure in the eastern and north eastern regions.
INLAND WATER TRANSPORT
(Recommendation at Para 73)
56.   The committee observes that the Government is giving step-motherly treatment to the Inland Water
 Transport Sector and this approach is reflected in the pattern of budgeting as well as utilization of funds in the
 IWT Sector. The Committee is dismayed to note that an outlay of Rs. 150.00 cr was allocated in BE 2005-06 for
 the IWT sector but it was reduced to Rs. 101.25 cr at RE stage and an expenditure of Rs. 47.87 cr was made only
 upto Feb. 2006. The Committee notes that Inland Water Transport is one of the oldest, economically,
 environmentally sustainable mode of transport but the potential of Inland Water Transport remains largely
 unexploited due to the detrimental policies of the Government. The Committee observes that although the
 Department of Shipping is committed to step up the share of IWT in the country’s total trade still this sector
 remains under developed at present for want of requisite infrastructure and therefore, is not viable for
 commercial operations. The Committee feels that inadequate policy support, interest and investments are some
 of the factors which are aggravating the problems of the Inland Water Transport and this sector is loosing a
 competitive edge with other modal mix in the country. The Committee is of the view that growth of the Inland
 Water Transport sector will entirely depend upon the quantum of investments, made through public-private
 partnership and a multi-dimensional approach for creating the required infrastructure primarily through
 Government support. The Committee, therefore, recommends the Department of Shipping to provide some
 institutional framework for creating a vibrant Inland Water Transport sector in the country and IWT should be
 included under the National Maritime Development Programme for augmentation of IWT fleet, creating of
 inter-modal linkages and up gradation of cargo handling technologies etc.

58.   Although IWAI has not been able to uitlise  all the budget allocated to it, the utilization has increased substantially.
 While IWAI expenditure was only Rs. 35 crores in eighth Plan, it has increased to about Rs. 151 crores in Ninth plan
 and to about 275 crores in the first four years of Tenth Plan.
59.   For 2006-07 there is an allocation of Rs. 150 crores for IWAI. IWAI has prepared detailed action plan for making
 three national waterways fully functional by March, 08 under which an investment of about Rs. 630 crores is estimated.
 Specific projects have been identified and IWAI is hopeful that the budget allocation would be fully utilized. The
 Department of Shipping has assured IWAI availability of fund will not be a constraint and more funds can be allocated
 based on need.
60.   It is also expected that after the three National waterways are made fully functional, commercial viability of IWT
 operations on these waterways will improve and then private sector will come forward to invest in ownership and
 operation of inland vessels and later on in development of infrastructure as well.
61.   Steps for encouraging private investment in IWT sector have nevertheless been initiated. Under these initiatives,
 three projects for construction of floating terminals for transportation of fly ash for Bangladesh  from Bandel, Budge-
Budge and Kolaghat in West Bengal have already been received from the prospective promoters. IWAI has also
 received bids from private sector for ownership and operation of cargo vessels on NW-1and 2 for identified O-D pairs
 of Kolkata-Mongla, Dhubri-Kolkata, Pandu-Kolkata and Dibrugarh-Kolkata. These are in process of approval from the
 Competent Authority.
62.   As far as institutional frame work is concerned, the-4WAI has already awarded a consultancy to National
 Productivity Council (NPC) for developing a better institutional frame work for development of IWT sector. Report
 from the National Productivity Council is expected to be submitted by Oct. 06. Government will be accordingly
 requested to take suitable action to strengthen IWAI for ensuring rapid development of the sector.
63.   As far as National Maritime Development Programme (NMDP) is concerned the development of inland water
 transport is already included as an important part of this programme under which projects related to IWT at an
 estimated cost of Rs. 10,500 crores have been proposed.
64.   The Hon’ble Prime Minister has also identified development of IWT as a thrust area under which it is envisaged to
 encourage gradual shift of domestic cargo from the rail and road modes to IWT, increasing its share from the present
 level of less than 1 per cent to atleast 2 per cent. Accordingly, IWAI has made following priorities for development of
 IWT. sector in the country:—
            (i)      Make three National Waterways fully functional
            (ii)      Promote cargo transportation by IWT mode - Modal shift of existing cargo and attracting new cargo.
            (iii)     Enable development of IWT fleet under private ownership.
            (iv)     Involve private sector in development, operation and management of IWT infrastructure.
            (v)     A Policy package for IWT Sector - Funds, Taxation, Incentives, positive discrimination.
            (vi)     Declaration and development of three new National Waterways.
            (vii)    Encourage States to develop their potential waterways through Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS).

 functional by March, 2008 with an estimated investment of about Rs.630 crore . The Committee also notes that
 the Department of Shipping has adopted several measures for encouraging private investment and developing
 institutional framework for IWT Sector in the country and Development of IWT has already been included
 under the National Maritime Development Programme. The Committee expects that after the three National
 waterways are made fully functional, commercial viability of IWT operations on these waterways will improve
 and then private sector will come forward to invest in ownership and operation of inland vessels and later on in
 development of infrastructure as well for the overall development and viability of this sector.

This Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Ministry of Civil Aviation on the
 observations/ recommendations as contained in its One-Hundred and Sixth Report on Demands for Grants (2006-07) of
 Ministry of Civil Aviation, which was presented to both the Houses of Parliament on 27th February, 2006.
 
 2.         Action Taken Replies have been received from the Ministry of Civil Aviation on 10 th November, 2006 in
 respect of all the observations/recommendations contained in the Report, which have been categorised as follows: -
 
(i)         Recommendations/observations, which have been accepted by the Ministry:
Para Nos. 15, 25, 32, 34, 68, 78, 92, 93, 99, 102, 118, 121, 133 &
139                                                                                                            Total- 14
(ii)        Recommendations/observations which the Committee does not desire to pursue in view of the Ministry’s
 replies:
Para No.                                                                                                          Nil.
(iii)       Recommendations/observations in respect of which replies of the Ministry have not been accepted by the
 Committee:
Para Nos. 19,  23, 27, 64, 73,  108, 123, 129, 141                                          Total- 9
(iv)       Recommendations/observations in respect of which final replies of the    Ministry are still awaited:
Para No. 20, 104, 135                                                                                                 3
 
3.         The Committee desires that final replies in respect of the recommendations, which have been categorized as
 interim replies by the Committee should be furnished to it at the earliest.
4.         On scrutiny of the said Action Taken Replies, the Committee has made observations on each item of Action
 taken/proposed to be taken by the Ministry.  The recommendations of the Committee contained in the One-Hundred
 and Sixth Report, action taken thereon by the Ministry, and recommendations/observations of the Committee on each
 item of action taken has been given in the succeeding paragraphs.
 
ASSESSMENT OF ANNUAL PLAN 2005-06 AND ALLOCATION FOR    2006-07
(Recommendation at Para 15)
 
5.         The Committee is happy to note that the Ministry has taken due cognizance of its earlier recommendations
 pertaining to utilisation of budget allocations and has made efforts to improve the earlier situation of consistent
 underutilization of funds.  The Committee notes that barring the low proportion of expenditure of Pawan Hans
 Helicopters Limited, the anticipated expenditure in respect of other organisations is satisfactory vis-a-vis the approved
 allocations.  The Committee, however expresses its concern that the Gross Budgetary Support has been reduced from
 Rs.370.85 crore in 2005-06 to Rs.130.00 crore in 2006-07.  The Committee expects that the targets set for internal and
 extra budgetary resources as well as external commercial borrowings from foreign banks/financial institutions for
 bridging the gap in budgetary support will materialize.  The Committee recommends that  the Ministry should take
 adequate steps during 2006-07 also to ensure optimum utilisation of the enhanced allocations made to various
 organisations.
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
 
6.         The reduction in Plan Outlay during 2006-07 was primarily due to the fact that no provision had been made for
 payment of budgetary support to Indian Airlines during 2006-07.  A provision of Rs.325 crores had been made during
 2005-06 for payment of budgetary support to Indian Airlines in connection with their aircraft acquisition project which
 was released during the year.  The balance expenditure on aircraft acquisition project was to be met by Indian Airlines
 out of their internal and extra budgetary resources including external commercial borrowings.  The observations of the

115 th Report of Committe on Industry
file:///D/responive/Committee%20on%20Transport,%20Tourism%20and%20Culture/115%20th%20Report.htm[22-10-2018 12:21:04]
 Committee with regard to optimum utilization plan allocations for 2006-07 have been noted for compliance.
 
 
AIR INDIA LIMITED
(Recommendation at Para 19)
 
7.         The Committee notes that the outlay for non-aircraft projects is an important component of the budget provision
 for Air India Limited as the programmes/projects undertaken there under viz. purchase of Ground Handling
 Equipments, Engineering Workshop Equipments, Security Equipments, Aircraft Refurbishment Programme etc. are
 aimed at enhancing the operational efficiency.   The Committee expects that the allocated funds would be fully utilised
 during 2006-07 and recommends that the Ministry should take suitable steps to ensure that the operational efficiency of
 Air India Limited is not compromised for want of funds.
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
 
8.         The recommendations of the Committee has been noted for compliance.  It would be ensured that operational
 efficiency of Air India Limited is not compromised for want of funds.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
 
9.         The Committee is not satisfied with the reply of the Ministry of Civil Aviation and desires to know actual details
 of the programmes/projects undertaken viz. purchase of Ground Handling Equipments, Engineering Workshop
 Equipments, Security Equipments, Aircraft Refurbishment Programme etc. and how much amount was spent on these
 projects out of the total outlay.  The Committee also desires the Ministry to furnish detail about the steps taken during
 the year to improve the operational efficiency of Air India Limited.
 
 
 
(Recommendation at 
Para 20)
 
10.       The Committee notes that Air India has been reporting net profits consistently since 2001-02 and expects that
 this healthy situation will continue. The Committee recommends that the Ministry should endeavour to focus on all the
 individual parameters that enhance the overall operational performance with the available aircraft capacity till new and
 modern aircraft join its fleet.
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
 
11.       The observations of the Committee have been noted.   Every endeavour is being made to enhance the operational
 performance of Air India to meet the ever increasing challenges in the aviation market.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
 
12.       The Committee desires that the recommendation should be taken seriously and reiterates its recommendation
 that the Ministry should endeavor to focus on all the individual parameters that enhance the overall operational
 performance with the available aircraft capacity till new and modern aircraft join its fleet.
 
(Recommendation at Para 23)
 
13.       The level of Passenger Load Factor has a direct impact on the profit/loss balance sheet. The Committee,
 therefore, recommends that Air India should adopt aggressive marketing strategies to improve its Passenger Load
 Factor to the desired level.  The Committee also recommends that the bilateral air services agreements should be
 leveraged to diversify the international air services and to avail the entitlements of new traffic rights to the full extent.
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT

115 th Report of Committe on Industry
file:///D/responive/Committee%20on%20Transport,%20Tourism%20and%20Culture/115%20th%20Report.htm[22-10-2018 12:21:04]
 
14.       Air India has been following aggressive marketing practices to improve its Passenger Load Factors, and
 consequently its revenue and profitability.  Some of measures undertaken by Air India are :
 
a)          Launching of a low cost carrier, Air India Express;
 
b)          Leasing of 28 aircraft (including 7 for Air India Express) to increase its market share and reach;
 
c)
          Acquisition of 68 new aircraft (including 18 for Air India Express) to improve the product and cut
 maintenance, fuel and other costs;
 
 
d)
          Introduction of non-stop flights, standardized timings, better connectivity from interior points in India;
 
e)
          Commenced direct marketing practices to reach customers personally;
 
f)
            Improvement in overall product with installation of flat beds in First Class and Soubrettes in Executive Class
 of all B747-400 aircraft and introduction of schemes like Premium Traveler Programme and Companion Free
 Scheme to improve utilization of First and Executive Class;
 
g)
          Introduction of customer friendly facilities like e-ticketing, advance check-in,   city check-in at Mumbai
 Airport, domestic and international call centers, etc;
 
h)
          Frequent Flyer Programme, Maharaja Club and Leading Edge Club to give high yield passengers recognition
 and value added benefits to retain their loyalty;.
 
15.       With the acquisition of new aircraft, Air India will have additional flights on routes which are commercially and
 economically viable, thus improving utilization of traffic rights.
 
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
 
16.       The Committee notes that the Air India has taken some measure to improve its passenger load factors.  However,
 the Committee takes exception to the fact that Ministry remains silent on its recommendation that the "bilateral air
 services agreements should be leveraged to diversify the international air services and to avail the entitlement of new
 traffic rights to the full extent."  The Committee desires to have action by the Ministry in the matter.
 
(Recommendation at 
Para 25)
 
17.       The Committee notes that important announcements have been made in the Annual Supplement, 2006 under the
 Foreign Trade Policy 2004-09, which inter-alia, will enable the country to offer competitive fuel prices and attract mid
 route stops for international flights and they are likely to play a catalytic role in the growth of civil aviation sector. The
 Committee recommends that the Ministry should pursue the matter regarding the issuance of notifications specifying
 the scope and extent of concessions/exemptions with the Commerce Ministry/Finance Ministry for deriving the
 anticipated benefits from the announcements made in the Annual Supplement, 2006 under the Foreign Trade Policy
 2004-09.   The Committee further recommends that the Ministry should initiate suitable steps in advance to facilitate
 the National Carriers to avail the full benefits of the announcements.
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
 
18.       Necessary provisions for allowing duty neutralization benefits to supply of stores on board foreign going
 aircraft, through Advance Authorisation Scheme, have been made in para 4.1.3 of the Foreign Trade Policy (2004-09). 
 Department of Revenue have also issued necessary instructions for implementation of this facility by the Customs
 authorities.  Since the entire scheme is intended to reduce the cost of stores for foreign going aircraft by neutralizing the

115 th Report of Committe on Industry
file:///D/responive/Committee%20on%20Transport,%20Tourism%20and%20Culture/115%20th%20Report.htm[22-10-2018 12:21:04]
 duty incidence on inputs required for manufacture of these goods, Air India, Indian Airlines and other airlines can
 obtain the benefits of this scheme through a proportionate cost reduction by the manufacturers of stores.  Air India and
 Indian Airlines are being advised to suitably negotiate with their suppliers.
 
(Recommendation at Para 27)
 
19.       The Committee notes that Air India had approached only M/s. Jet Airways in July, 2005 to negotiate the wet-
lease of one A340-330E aircraft.  The Committee is of the opinion that Air India could have approached other Airlines
 organisations.  The procedure followed by Air India was against the practice of open competitive tendering process and
 therefore lacks transparency.  The Committee feels that the impending shortage could have been anticipated early had
 there been a constant assessment of the available aircraft capacity. The Committee further recommends that adequate
 contingency plans should be prepared including standing arrangements for lease of aircraft during exigencies by
 following the proper tendering process.
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
 
20.       The lease of aircraft by Air India from Jet Airways was a very short term arrangement.   However, observations
 of the Committee in this regard have been noted by Air India for future guidance. 
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
 
21.       The Committee is not satisfied with the reply of the Ministry of Civil Aviation and desires to know whether
 there are any policy/guidelines for leasing of aircraft. The Committee recommends and directs that a market oriented
 transparent tender process should be formulated for leasing of aircraft either for short term or long term arrangements.
 
INDIAN AIRLINES LIMITED
(Recommendation at 
Para 32)
 
22.       The Committee notes that there is a scope for further improvement in the overall load factor of Indian Airlines
 and recommends that there is a need to focus attention of all the factors that are responsible for acting as constraints in
 the achievement of the desired level of overall load factor.   The Committee also notes with concern that the market
 share of national carriers has decreased despite the overall increase in the growth rate of domestic passengers' traffic,
 which is also reflected in the decline in the reported profits of Indian Airlines.  The Committee recommends that
 adequate steps, in addition to the acquisition of aircraft, should be taken to enable Indian Airlines to tap the market
 opportunities in the domestic as well as international markets.
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
 
23.       Overall Load Factor of Indian Airlines in the past few years has shown an increasing trend as can be seen from
 the statistics provided below:-
 
 
      Period
           Load Factor (%)
2003-04                 65.4
2004-05              68.6
2005-06              71.4
 
24.       Capacity share of Indian Airlines in the domestic market has been declining with the induction of capacity by the
 competitors and due to the reason that Indian Airlines has not been able to match its competitors in this regard.  
 Consequently IA’s market share has also tended to decline.    Airlines the world over experience a similar direct
 correlation between their capacity share and market share.   Indian Airlines has made efforts to retain its capacity share
 by leasing of aircraft pending renewal/augmentation of fleet through outright purchase route.  The aircraft that Indian
 Airlines has leased in the recent years have largely served to replace some of the aging A300 aircraft that have been
 phased out by the airline during this period.   

115 th Report of Committe on Industry
file:///D/responive/Committee%20on%20Transport,%20Tourism%20and%20Culture/115%20th%20Report.htm[22-10-2018 12:21:04]
 
25.       Due to inordinate delay in the finalization of IA’s fleet acquisition programme the average age of IA’s fleet
 compares quite unfavourably with that of its competitors’.    The travelling public perceive an older aircraft to be an
 inferior product and consequently IA's services have not been quite as appealing to some of the passengers and as such
 they prefer the services offered by IA's competitors.   
 
26.       Indian Airlines takes continuous measures to improve its services and product offered to its passengers.   Some
 of the measures taken to improve services and product upgrades are as follows:-
-
          Schedule upgrades and capacity increases.
-          Special fares/schemes on the Domestic sectors and dynamic market fares as well as incentives on
 international sectors.
-          Sales and marketing initiatives.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
 
27.       The Committee notes that despite increase in the overall load factor, market share of the Indian Airlines has gone
 down.  The Committee hopes that after acquisition of fleet, the share of Indian Airlines in the market will also improve.
 
(Recommendation at 
Para 34)
 
28.       The Committee feels that the issue of wage revision of employees of Indian Airlines has been pending for a long
 time. In this connection, the Committee would like to draw the attention of the Ministry to the recommendations made
 by the Committee in its 96
th Report, which is reproduced below: -
 
“The Committee expresses its anguish over the evasive comments of the Ministry offered in response to the
 recommendation of the Parliamentary Committee.  The Committee is extremely unhappy about the lackadaisical
 approach of the Ministry on the issue of revision of scales of pay of employees of Indian Airlines.  The
 Committee is of the view that the satisfaction level of the personnel in the matter of service conditions is a
 major factor affecting the performance of any organisation.  The total inaction on the part of the Ministry in the
 matter of pay revision of employees of Indian Airlines is surprising, especially in the present age of poaching
 and stiff competition by other Indian scheduled carriers.  The Committee, therefore, reiterates that the Ministry
 should expedite its decision in the matter in the overall interest of the employees and the organisation.”   The
 Committee once again reiterates the above recommendation and expects an early action thereon.
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
 
29.       Wage revisions up to 31.12.1996 in respect of all categories of employees in Indian Airlines had been completed
 in 2001.   Further, Productivity Linked Incentive (PLI) Schemes, which had been introduced in 1994, were revised in
 1996 and further revised in respect of all categories of employees from the year 2001. There has been substantial
 increase in emoluments consequent to payments under the Productivity Linked Incentive Schemes based on
 improvement in pre-determined productivity parameters.   The revised PLI Settlement in respect of non-technical
 categories of employees represented by the Air Corporation Employee’s Union (ACEU) was last signed on 23.3.2004.
 
30.       Indian Airlines had taken a decision in December 1999 that considering the financial position of the Company
 and increasing competitive pressures, there was no justification for increase in wages at that stage. 
 
31.       Subsequently,  Air India entered into a settlement with Air India Employees Guild for wage revision effective
 01.01.1997, a comprehensive note has been received  from Indian Airlines Ltd., requesting the Ministry for issuance of
 appropriate directions as per the guidelines.  Requisite directive has since been issued to Indian Airlines to commence
 wage negotiations with their Unions/Associations on 21.7.2006. 
 
 
ACQUISITION OF AIRCRAFT BY INDIAN AIRLINES LIMITED & AIR INDIA LIMITED

 the delivery of aircraft to Indian Airlines and Air India are adhered to so that the National Carriers are able to take
 maximum benefits of exemption from payment of tax under Section 10(15A).  The Committee hopes that the Ministry

 adhere to the agreed timeframe of delivery of aircraft.  The Committee recommends the Government to ensure that the
 commitments made by the M/s. Boeing and M/s. Airbus Industrie to set up training centers for flight and maintenance

 is further recommended that the matter regarding the extension beyond 1

34.       The Union Budget 2006 extended the exemption from with-holding tax on lease of aircraft and aircraft engines
 for a further period of one year i.e. lease agreements executed on or before 31.3.2007 would be exempted from levy of
 with-hold tax.  The proposal for further continuation of this exemption would be taken up with Ministry of Finance at

 companies for the supply of aircraft.

(Recommendation at 
Para 78)

 tourist places.  The Committee recommends that Pawan Hans Helicopters Limited should prepare specific plans to

73.       The policy of opening up of international skies to Indian scheduled airlines was adopted to ensure full realization
 of the objective to enhance utilisation of traffic rights available to India.  The Committee however notes that despite the
 permission granted to private carriers to operate services to USA and Belgium, the services have not commenced and it
 is surprising that the Ministry has left the matter to the commercial judgement of the concerned airlines.  The
 Committee is of the view that there should be proper monitoring of the permissions granted by the Ministry and
 recommends that it must be ensured that actual operations are started by the operators so that the stated objective of
 optimum utilisation of traffic rights is achieved.  The Committee also reiterates its recommendations contained in its
 96
th Report, which is reproduced below: -
 
“The Committee notes from the reply of the Ministry that there are only two minimum eligibility criteria
 prescribed for selection of scheduled domestic airlines to be allowed to operate on international routes, namely,
 a minimum fleet strength of 20 aircraft and a minimum experience of five years operations on domestic routes. 
 The Committee also notes that the basic policy of the Government to allow the scheduled carriers to operate on
 international routes has been framed after due consideration of the Report of Naresh Chandra Committee, which
 was submitted to the Ministry in December 2003.  The said committee had reportedly revealed that we are
 presently using only 40% of our bilateral rights.  However, the Committee feels that the steep restrictions
 imposed by the Ministry are impediments in achieving the basic objectives behind the new policy to mitigate
 under capacity in the international segment and to enhance global connectivity to and from different states in the
 country.   The Committee recommends that in view of the irreversible nature of the new policy, the Ministry

74.       Commencement of actual operations may not only be a commercial decision of the airlines, but approval of the

 allowed to operate on international routes, the Ministry has already clarified the position.  For operations of scheduled
 flights on the domestic sector, the requirement of minimum fleet strength is 5 aircraft, which is considered adequate for
 providing reliable schedule services on regional routes.  It is not possible to provide reliable schedule services on metro
 routes with 5 aircraft.  It is believed that more than 10 aircraft would be needed to provide reliable schedule services on
 metro routes.  For international operations the operator must have a proper network for providing services within India
 on metro, regional and sub-regional routes.  It was in this context that it was considered essential that an airline, which
 is permitted to operate on international routes must have a minimum of 20 aircraft.

96.       It may further be stated that Kingfisher Airlines, SpiceJet and Air Deccan have initiated measures for training of
 their pilots for CAT-II operations after complying with the Civil Aviation Requirements.  These airlines have been
 granted Initial Authorization for CAT-II operations.
 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE
           
97.       The Committee is not satisfied with the approach of the Ministry of Civil Aviation in the matter of utilization of
 CAT II/III system installed at IGI Airport, New Delhi.  Because of the lethargic approach of the Government, the
 investment made on the installation of CAT III system going waste and the past experience of most of the private
 carriers during the foggy conditions show abysmal picture.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that Ministry of
 Civil Aviation should take action against private carriers who are not imparting training to their pilot in CAT through
 ILS.  So, that the CAT III instruments installed at Delhi Airport should be used in an optimal manner.
 
 
BENCHMARKING OF AIRPORTS
(Recommendation at 
Para 133)
 
98.       The Committee notes that the although there are certain pre-requisites for declaration of an airport as
 international airport, the term world class airport is an objective term depending on the availability of facilities
 comparable to major airports in the region.  The Committee is, therefore, of the opinion that the airports declared as
 international airports in the country will not certainly be of world class standards unless passenger friendly facilities are
 developed.  In this context, the Committee notes that the customer satisfaction survey has revealed that overall
 satisfaction level with Mumbai International Airport, Delhi International Airport and Delhi Domestic Airport are well
 below the desired standard of 3.5 on a five point scale and also the average obtaining in airports in the Middle East/Asia
 Pacific region.  Only the figures in respect of Mumbai Domestic  Airport are near to the desired standard of 3.5 and the
 average obtaining in airports in the Middle East/Asia Pacific region.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that there
 is a need to develop suitable institutional mechanism to assess the performance standards on continuous basis and take
 steps to upgrade the same to world-class standards.
 
REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT
 
99.       Airports Authority of India has already initiated action for upgrading, improvement and modernization of
 infrastructure facilities at the international airport at non-metro cities in addition to domestic airports in a phased
 manner.  Global Technical Advisor (GTA) has been engaged for suggesting improvement in the facilities as per world
 class standards.   New terminal buildings will have all the passengers' friendly facilities of world class standards.  The
 designs are being adopted as per the yardsticks recommended by International Air Transport Association (IATA) and
 International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO). Special care has also been taken for handling of physically
 challenged passengers.  For them, special design toilets, ramp areas at various places for movement of wheel chairs,
 provision of Ambu-lift and wheel chairs by AAI as well as Airline operator would be ensured.  In addition AAI is also
 providing passengers boarding bridges in the new terminal buildings alongwith escalators and elevators.
 
100.     With effect from the effective date i.e. 3.5.2006, the responsibility to operate, maintain, develop, design,
 construct, upgrade, modernize, financing and management of Chhatarpati Shivaji International Airport, Mumbai and

 Indira Gandhi International Airport, New Delhi has been transferred to Joint Venture Companies in accordance with
 Operation, Management and Development Agreement between JVCs and AAI.
 
101.     However, with a view to upgrade the standard and ultimately customer satisfaction level at other international
 airports, the concerned  Airport Director / Officer-in-Charge have been informed about  the parameter(s) / facility(ies)
 where the rating had been below the acceptable level and also to find ways and means to improve the same.
 
ALLOTMENT OF PARKING BAYS
(Recommendation at 
Para 135)
 
102.     The Committee notes that the Airports Authority of India is in the process of developing a policy on the
 allotment of night parking bays to various airlines and additional parking bays are being constructed at various airports
 in the country to meet the demand.  The Committee recommends that the policy should be formulated at the earliest and
 the work relating to construction of additional parking bays at various airports should be completed within a stipulated
 time frame.  The Committee also expects that the airline operators would avail the concessions offered by the Ministry
 to decongest the bigger airports.

103.     In the past, major demand in respect of overnight parking stands has been for Delhi and Mumbai airports. These
 two airports have been handed over to JVCs w.e.f. 3.5.2006 for development, management & operation. The JVCs shall
 be allotting night parking stands at these two airports.
 
104.     In respect of other airports the draft policy for allotment of parking stands is under formulation in AAI. The list
 of apron works presently in planning stage and works in progress are given at Appendix A and B respectively.
 
105.     4 Nos. additional parking bays are under construction at Kolkata, while for another 8 bays, tenders are being
 called.
 
106.     20 Nos. additional parking bays are under construction at Chennai Airport. All efforts are being made to
 complete the works within this financial year.

107.     The Committee notes the reply.  The Committee desires that a copy of the draft policy for allotment of parking
 stands should be given to the Committee as and when it is finalised by the AAI.

 Committee recommends that the signing of the Memoranda of Understanding with various Ministries to ensure that a
 large part of Government of India personnel travel on Air India should be completed at the earliest so that the hitherto
 assured revenue will remain with the organisation.   The Committee notes that the special package of Leave Travel
 Concession to Government of India personnel to visit Jammu and Kashmir expires in June 2006 and therefore
 recommends that the Ministry should provide additional flights till such period to the extent possible in view of the
 non-availability of accommodation in the present flight schedule.

109.     With a view to capturing the high yield Government of India business, Air India has been negotiating with
 various Ministries to ensure that their personnel travel abroad only on Air India’s services, by way of offering a

 services provided by the airlines operators.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the National Civil Aviation
 Policy should be formulated and announced at the earliest to address the complex issues prevalent in the civil aviation
 sector of the country.

 development and regulation of civil aviation in the country and for devising and implementing schemes for orderly
 growth and expansion of civil air transport.  Its functions also extend to overseeing the provision of airport facilities, air
 traffic services, carriage of passengers and goods by air, safeguarding civil aviation operations, regulation of air
 transport services, licensing of aerodromes, air carriers, pilots and aircraft maintenance engineers. In addition to
 framing policies, the Ministry provides guidance to the organisations in the implementation of policy guidelines. It
 supervises implementation by the organisations of special programmes of the Government, particularly those intended
 for weaker sections.  The Ministry also administratively controls the Commission of Railway Safety, a statutory body

MERGER OF AIR INDIA LIMITED AND INDIAN AIRLINES LIMITED
46.       The Ministry was specifically asked about the merger of Air India and Indian Airlines Ltd.  In its response, the
 Ministry has stated that the Government has decided to merge the two airlines into a new company, which would
 further strengthen the public sector airlines.  The new airline would be the largest airline in the country comparable to
 other airlines in Asia and will provide an integrated international and national footprint.   The merger would enable
 these two airlines to pool their resources, achieve synergies, face competition and establish fresh benchmarks for
 efficiency and reliability.   The merger of the two airlines would be completed in a phased manner over the next two
 years.
47.       The Ministry has also stated that the merger is in keeping with the industry trend of moving towards
 consolidation and mergers enabling the airlines to achieve synergies and reduce costs.  The merged airline would be
 able to offer an integrated schedule from interior points in the country(currently served by Indian) to various
 international destinations (currently served by Indian and/or Air India) and vice-versa, offering seamless connectivity to
 passengers and also extending the connectivity of interior points to various international destinations via the major hub
 airports in India. 
48.       A bigger and stronger public sector national carrier will also help in expanding regional connectivity to hitherto
 under-serviced and un-serviced destinations.   While taking the merger decision, employees interests have been
 accorded prime importance.   The Government is committed to ensure that all legitimate interests of employee,
 including their current compensations, status, etc. are protected.   There will be no retrenchment and all employees of
 both the airlines will continue in the merged company.  The exercise of integrating manpower would be completed in a
 phased manner, on the basis of transparent and objective criteria.  A well-defined Grievance Redressal Machinery will
 also be put in place.
49.       The Committee raised the question on the issue of extra expenditure to be incurred on completing the process on
 which the Secretary, stated as under:
"Sir, there would be cost of the integration merger.   But the consultants have given a roadmap which indicates that on
 balance, there would a saving because there would be savings in terms of synergies, savings in terms of avoidance of
 duplication, etc.  So, at the end of the third year, there would be a saving of Rs.400 crore, taking into account the extra
 costs involved in the higher pay scales, etc".
50.       The Committee also expressed its concern over the issue of positioning of employees of both the carriers in the
 new entity for which the Secretary stated as under:
"Sir, I would be less than honest if I say that there will be no problems.  The HR issues in any merger cause problems,
 and when you have two large entities with 18,000 plus employees and 15,000 plus employees, it certainly not going to
 be an easy task.  But apart from the fact that there will be no retrenchment and nobody would lose his job and so which
 is the most basis thing, what the employees have been assured is that there will be a three-tier grievance redressal
 machinery which will be put in place..."

 international market.   The Committee hopes that the synergisation process would help to improve the operational

 we should be able to have a clear cut civil aviation policy vision 2020".
54.       The Committee notes that the present civil aviation sector needs a well balanced and market oriented policy to
 address all the issues relating to the boom in passenger and cargo traffic.  The quantum of increase in passenger traffic
 needs strict enforcement of safety and security related issues.  The Committee, however, is constrained to note that
 Ministry of Civil Aviation has not come out with a Civil Aviation Policy till date. Now the Government plans to have a
 policy with a vision for 2020.  The Committee hopes that the policy will be in place soon and take care of all the issues
 relating to civil aviation sector of current as well as future era.
RESTRUCTURING OF DELHI AND MUMBAI AIRPORTS
55.       The Committee was informed that the Government on 1
st February, 2006 finalized the restructuring and
 modernization of the two international airports at Delhi and Mumbai through public-private partnership in the joint-
venture mode.  In the joint venture, Airports Authority of India(AAI) holds 26% equity and the remaining 74% is held
 by the strategic partner i.e. GMR consortium for Delhi airport and GVK consortium for Mumbai airport.  Foreign
 Direct Investment (FDI) in this transaction has been capped at 49%.  It has been estimated on preliminary basis that the
 capital investment to the extent of Rs.7961 crores and Rs.6161 crores will be required for Delhi and Mumbai airports
 respectively over a period of l20 years, in 4 stages of l5 years each.  The two international airports have been handed
 over to the Joint Venture Companies(JVCs), namely, Delhi International Airport Private Limited(DIAL) and Mumbai
 International Airport Private Limited(MIAL) respectively on 3rd May, 2006.  These JVcs have taken over the complete
 operational control on 3rd November, 2006.   These two JVcs have submitted their proposal to the Government for the
 development of Delhi and Mumbai airports.
56.       While scrutinizing the outcome budget of the Ministry for the year 2006-07 the Committee finds that a
 substantial amount of money has been spent by the AAI for repair and maintenance work at international airports at
 Delhi and Mumbai even after these two airports were handed over to the JVCs in May, 2006.  The Committee desires
 to know the reasons for this and also wants to know the expenditure incurred by the JVCs on the respective airports for
 maintenance and up keep of airports till date.
57.       A Tripartite Committee with the representatives of Ministry of Civil Aviation, Airports Authority of India and
 AAI Employees Joint Forum has been constituted by the Ministry of Civil Aviation on     22
nd February, 2006 to look
 into the issues and proposals of modernizing airports by Airports Authority of India and employees related issues
 including job security.  The Committee desires to know the details of meetings which have been taken so far with the
 decisions arrived therein.  The Committee also reiterates its recommendation contained in its 106
th Report that the
 Tripartite Committee should hold regular meetings and finalise its Report in a time bound manner in view of the

 and Kolkata airports on priority basis.  They have listed out various planned activities for modernization and

71/2 million passengers per year.... so, up gradation of the airport in a time-bound manner is very, very important and

SHORTAGE AND TRAINING OF PILOTS
63.       About the steps taken by the Ministry to overcome the shortage of pilots which is a major deterrent in the
 expansion of civil aviation sector  the Committee was informed  that due to the entry of new airlines and expansions of
 fleet by the existing airlines, the industry is facing acute shortage of qualified personnel, especially, Pilots and Flying
 Instructors.  To meet this demand, a project for upgradation of existing training facilities at IGRUA, at an estimated
 cost of 21.82 crores, has been sanctioned in September, 2006.  Other proposal of augmentation of training facilities like
 acquisition of single and multi engine aircraft and modern training equipment is under active consideration.
64.       The Government proposes to establish a premier pilot training institute at Gondia, Maharashtra to augment the
 ongoing efforts to Flying Training Schools for increasing the number of qualified and well trained pilots.  Airport
 Authority of India has taken over land measuring 405.92 hectares from the State Government, for this purpose.  It has
 been decided that the new Flying Training School would eventually be a Joint Venture project with the participation of
 all stakeholders.  Airport Authority of India would have a equity participation of 49% which can be shared amongst the
 other aviation related PSUs.  Airport Authority of India is in the process of finalization of JV partner and "Expression
 of Interest" (EOI) has been invited.

UNIFORM TAXATION OF ATF     
66.       During the course of the oral evidence of the representatives of Ministry of Civil Aviation, the Committee was
 informed that the domestic air transport industry of the nation has been facing serious problems due to high costs of
 operations. One of the major reasons for this is the heavy cost of Air Turbine Fuel (ATF).  Even though the pricing of
 ATF is now on import parity basis, the rates applicable for domestic operations continue to be significantly higher than
 that of international operations.  The cost of ATF goes up even further due to high rates of sales tax levied by the State
 Governments/Union Territory Administration varying from 25 per cent to 30 per cent which affects the viability of
 domestic airline operations.
67.       The Secretary, while tendering his evidence also raised this issue  before the Committee  and stated as under:
".....Sir, as you aware, is a very important and a major component of the variable cost of operations.   Sir, the cost in
 India, the way it is priced and the way there is excise duty and , then there is Sales Tax in the States, is much higher, at
 least 25-30 per cent higher than what it is overseas.  We have been requesting that at least it be notified as a declared
 good under section 14 of the Central Sales Tax Act for all types of aircraft; so that there is a cap on the quantum of levy
 which can be imposed on this.  Sir, presently it is four per cent; ...... we have got some relief in relation to smaller
 aircraft, but it is not yet available for the aviation sector and all the operators, as a whole".
 
68.       The Ministry was asked about the budget proposal to amend the Central Sales Tax to treat aviation turbine fuel
 as a declare goods for all small aircraft with a maximum take of less than 40,000 kg operated by scheduled carriers and
 also the impact of this amendment on the aviation sector for which the ministry replied that until now, this facility was
 available only to turbo-prop aircraft.   The present proposal to extend the concession to all small aircraft including jet
 aircraft operated by scheduled airlines would encourage and facilitate connectivity to non-metro and other smaller cities
 by more efficient small jet aircraft.
 
69.       The Cost of fuel is an important component of cost structure and has direct bearing on the profitability of any
 airline. High cost of ATF in the country increases the cost of operation of carriers which results in escalation in the
 airfares.  The Committee recommends that Ministry of Finance should sympathetically consider and give approval to
 the proposal of Ministry of Civil Aviation regarding notifying ATF as 'Declared Good' under Section 14 of Central
 Sales Tax Act on priority basis to all the aircraft  so that sales tax on ATF could be contained with the maximum rate of
 4%. The Committee further recommends that the Ministry of Finance may also discuss the issue with the State
 Governments and try to pursuade them to reduce   the sales tax on ATF.  The Committee feels that restructuring the
 excise duty on ATF will have a positive impact on the development of civil aviation sector of the nation.
UTILISATION OF CAT III SYSTEM AT DELHI AIRPORT
70.       During the winter season, the air passengers are put into great hardship by cancellation/diversion of flights due
 to fog at Delhi airport.  The Committee sought the remedial actions proposed to avoid such a situation during the next
 year. The Ministry in its reply stated that the airlines are encouraged to upgrade their aircraft and train their pilots for
 operations in low visibility conditions.   Their flight schedules are approved on the basis of number of pilots trained by
 the operators for low visibility operations and the suitability of the planes for such operations.   If the operator cannot
 provide data for their capability to fly under low visibility, they are not allowed to schedule their flights during normal
 fog hours.  The Ministry also stated that airlines have been directed not to roster their CAT III trained pilots on
 international routes during the fog season.  DGCA also requires that the airlines should train their pilots for ILS CAT
 II/III operations.   Pilots who are CAT II/III qualified are approved as Instructor/Examiner so as to ensure that more
 trained pilots are available for CAT II/III operations during low visibility conditions. 
71.       The Committee is constrained to note that a huge investment has been made in installation of ILS CAT-III
 facilities at IGI airport.  However there is a lot of delay or cancellation of flights due to fog as there are not enough
 pilots trained to operate the flights during fog. It appears that steps taken by the Government in this regard have proved
 inadequate. The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry that Airlines have been directed not to roster their CAT III
 trained pilots on international routes during fog season and also recommended that  training of pilots to fly on low
 visibility conditions be extended to a maximum number of pilots in both the national carriers. The Committee
 recommends that strict penal provisions should be imposed on the airlines which are failing to give proper training to

 level except for the year 2006-07.  The Committee feels that the Civil Aviation sector has now become vibrant
 component of our economy and any laxity in utilisation of plan outlay can affect the development of the economy. The
 Committee ,therefore, recommends that the Ministry of Civil Aviation should ensure that all its organisations do utilise
 the allocated funds to the maximum extent in order to maintain its upper hand in the Civil Aviation sector where stiff
 competition is expected in the coming years due to the entry of more private players in the domestic and International
 arena.  The Committee hopes that this positive trend of utilisation of allocated outlay will continue during the 11
th Five
 Year Plan also.   (Para 6)
ASSESSMENT OF ANNUAL PLAN 2006-07 AND ALLOCATION FOR 2007-08
The Committee notes that except the Airports Authority of India, anticipated expenditure in respect of all other
 organizations is satisfactory. The Committee reiterates that the Ministry should ensure that all the organizations under
 its control utilize the approved outlay optimally.   The Committee desires that the utilization of external and internal
 budget resources for the acquisition of aircraft for Air India and Indian Airlines take place systematically.   The
 Committee also recommends that proper exercise should be done to identify the likely expenditure involved in the
 merger of Indian Airlines and Air-India and provision therefor should be made accordingly in the Budget at RE
 stage.
